data.name: Celedonia
data.long_meaning: From the Latin word celidonius, meaning heavenly, celestial, or sky-blue. Derived from the Greek word keladon, meaning celery, which shares the same root as the word celestial. In mythology, Celedonia was the Roman goddess of the moon and the night, and was also known as the goddess of fertility and the protector of travelers.

data.numerology_meaning: Encourages a balance between the material and spiritual worlds. Inspires creativity and a deep connection with nature. Representative of nurturing, maternal, and caring energies.

data.cultural_impact: The name Celedonia comes from the Roman culture, which has influenced Western civilization significantly. The association of Celedonia with the moon and night reflects the Roman belief in the importance of observing and understanding the natural world. It also highlights the ancient Roman practice of personifying natural phenomena and assigning them deities. Today, the name Celedonia can evoke a sense of mystery, tranquility, and connection to the natural world and the night sky.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Celedonia can be spiritually significant as a reminder of God's presence and protection in the night. The reference to Celedonia as the goddess of fertility and the protector of travelers reflects the Christian belief in God as the giver of life and the one who watches over and protects his people on their journeys. The celestial and heavenly significance of the name can also symbolize the spiritual journey toward God and the eternal life in heaven.
